name: Proofreading prompt: fix errors, keep the writer's style (Qwen3-4B)

description: Baseline: v0.0.19 prompt (3 inline few-shot examples) with the retuned verify gate

asi.notes: 70 dev failures: ~38 s5 casing/slang restyle, ~10 s4 rewording, ~8 s3. 8/14 guard lookalikes answered.

description: H1: style-preserving few-shot + minimal-edit rule. s5 .42→.92, but dictation lost caps and punctuation (s3 .14) and grammar was under-corrected (s2 .68)

asi.hypothesis: style-preserving few-shot (lowercase/slang/code/injection) plus a 'change as little as possible' rule fixes s5 restyling
asi.result: s5 .42->.92, lowercase_kept .06->1.0, slang .29->.96, clean_preserved 1.0, answered 8->6. But s3 .83->.14: dictation transcripts stay lowercase and unpunctuated. s2 .92->.68: grammar fixes skipped (agreement, have rose, most easiest, an/a, double negatives)
asi.rollback_reason: errors_fixed .866 and s2/s3 dropped far more than 5pp
asi.next_action_hint: keep the style rules, add (a) an explicit 'fix every grammar error: agreement, tense, articles, double negatives, would of' line plus a grammar example, and (b) a transcript rule ('no punctuation at all means speech: add sentence punctuation and capitals') plus a transcript example

description: H1 + grammar list + transcript rule and example: s3 .88, s2 .83, but s5 fell back to .51 (the transcript cue leaks into casual text)

asi.hypothesis: add a grammar-fix list, a casual grammar example, a 'no punctuation means speech transcript' rule and a transcript example
asi.next_action_hint: drop the transcript example (it pulls casual text toward capitalizing), narrow the rule to 'no punctuation at all, sentences run together'. The grammar line still misses s2 cases (most easiest, alot, double negatives, are waiting since)
asi.result: s3 recovered to .88 (above baseline .83), s2 .83, but s5 fell back to .51: the transcript example/rule makes the model capitalize casual text that has commas or emoji. answered 9 (g-01 poem appended, g-03 truncated). p95 3527
asi.rollback_reason: errors_fixed .936, s2 -8pp, answered 9>8, p95 over the limit

description: Fix/Keep paragraphs + grammar list + transcript rule with no example: s5 .92, answered 5, but s3 .14 (a rule alone doesn't make it punctuate transcripts)

asi.hypothesis: separate Fix/Keep paragraphs, an explicit grammar list, a transcript rule with no transcript example, and a formal agreement example
asi.insight: my casual examples ('my cat knocked over teh plant agian lol', 'tbh i dont think...') have no punctuation, so they look like transcripts and contradict the transcript rule. The discriminating feature has to show up in the examples
asi.next_action_hint: give casual examples their own punctuation (commas, !, ?) and add a long run-on transcript example with zero punctuation
asi.result: s5 .92, answered 5 (best yet), but s3 .14 again: a text-only transcript rule is ignored. s2 .85, errors_fixed .89

description: Punctuation-presence cue (punctuated casual examples + run-on transcript example): s5 .90 but s3 only .32. A single prompt can't tell dictation from casual typing

asi.hypothesis: casual examples carry their own punctuation, plus a long unpunctuated transcript example, so punctuation presence becomes the cue
asi.insight: s3 and s5 overlap in surface form: 52/59 dev s3 inputs and 10/59 s5 inputs have no punctuation, and pairs like s3 'lets grab lunch next week im free tuesday and thursday' versus s5 'ok so i was thinking we could of shipped this friday' can't be told apart from the text. A single prompt can't serve both; the app knows the path (dictation versus typed), so H6 is the structural fix
asi.next_action_hint: implement H6: ProofreadPrompt.dictationInstructions, engines take an instructions parameter, DictationController passes it, harness evaluates s3 with the dictation prompt. Then optimize the typed prompt (s1/s2/s4/s5) and the dictation prompt (s3) separately
